sections.h2: Which office handles property tax in Lenoir County?
sections.html:
The Lenoir County Tax Department, at 101 North Queen Street in Kinston, lists, appraises and bills all property in the county. Call 252-527-7174. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

Its records cover real estate, personal property, property transfers, exemptions, exclusions and deferrals. The department also keeps the county land records and GIS mapping, bills special taxing districts such as fire districts, municipal service districts and drainage districts, and administers solid waste fees, privilege licenses and permits to move mobile homes.

The county website has links to view and pay tax bills, look up real property records, schedule a real property appeal, and file business or individual personal property listings. A seller checking a bill before closing can start there, then call the office for a payoff figure.

sections.h2: When are Lenoir County property taxes due and when does interest start?
sections.html:
Taxes are due September 1, and a bill paid before January 6 carries no interest. From January 6 to February 1 the interest is 2 percent, and after that it runs at 3/4 percent per month or part of a month until paid.

A mailed payment is treated as received on its U.S. Postal postmark date.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Lenoir County property value?
sections.html:
Appeals of real estate values go to the Lenoir County Board of Equalization and Review, and the window for the 2026 appeals closed on April 23, 2026, when the board adjourned. The county says the appeal window for 2027 opens on January 1, 2027.

That board is a quasi-judicial body under G.S. 105-322. It hears disputes about the listing and appraisal of real estate, individual and business personal property, applications for exemption, requests for exclusion and present-use value classifications.

To appeal, request a hearing in writing or by personal appearance before the board adjourns. The board mails its decision within 30 days after adjournment. If you still disagree, a written notice of appeal to the state Property Tax Commission must be filed within 30 days after the date the board mailed its notice, with a copy to the county assessor. The Lenoir County site has a link to schedule a real property appeal.

sections.h2: When did Lenoir County last revalue property?
sections.html:
The county's page says values stayed the same from the reappraisal effective January 1, 2017, and it described the next reappraisal as effective January 1, 2025. State law requires counties to reappraise real property at least every eighth year, as of January 1 of the scheduled year.

Between those dates, the assessed value does not move with the market. It changes when the property itself changes, such as new construction or a removed building. The county explains that a reappraisal updates every property's market value as of its effective date, with certified appraisers visiting properties and checking characteristics, market sales and costs.

For a seller, the practical point is that the value on the tax bill is not a sale price. Compare your latest notice with recent sales before you decide on an asking price, and ask the tax office for the current assessed value of your parcel.

sections.h2: What property tax relief programs exist for Lenoir County owners?
sections.html:
North Carolina has three homestead programs, and the county accepts the applications on Form AV-9. An owner may take benefit from only one of them. Applications should be filed during the listing period, but they must be accepted through June 1 before the tax year.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or 50 percent of the home's appraised value, for owners 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled, with income at or under the limit. The limit is $38,800 for the 2026 tax year.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income limit, on Form NCDVA-9 filed with the assessor.
  • Circuit breaker: tax capped at 4.0 percent of income when income is up to the limit, or 5.0 percent when it is over the limit up to 150 percent of it. Five years of owning and occupying the home is required, and a new application is needed each year.

Land used for farming, horticulture or forestry may qualify for the present-use value program, which gives a reduced assessment. Lenoir County has an AV-7 request form for an estimate of deferred taxes. Ask the office for that estimate before you sell qualified land.

sections.h2: What happens to Lenoir County property tax when I sell?
sections.html:
The tax lien attaches to the parcel as of the January 1 listing date, so the bill follows the property. A closing attorney or title company normally asks the Lenoir County Tax Department for the current balance and pays it from the sale proceeds at the table.

For personal property the rule is different. A lien for personal property taxes attaches to all of the taxpayer's real property in the taxing unit, so unpaid boat, aircraft or business equipment bills can show up against a house. Individual personal property such as boats, jet skis, aircraft, mobile homes and unlicensed vehicles must be listed every January, and a listing after January 31 draws a 10 percent penalty.

Lenoir County uses a permanent listing system for real estate, so a seller does not relist the house each year unless the value changed.

sections.h2: What if I fall behind on taxes in Lenoir County?
sections.html:
Unpaid real estate taxes are collected by a foreclosure action in the nature of a mortgage foreclosure, filed in the county where the property lies. The owner of record, the spouse and other lienholders are served.

The sale is a public auction at the courthouse door. The commissioner may require a deposit of up to 20 percent of the bid, and the sale reports within three days. Exceptions or an increased bid may be filed within 10 days after the report, and the commissioner's fee can reach 5 percent of the purchase price. Before the sale is confirmed, a person redeeming pays the taxes due plus penalties, interest and costs.

The county tax page lists a legal services contact for tax foreclosures. If a notice has arrived, call the Lenoir County tax office and a legal aid provider early.

sections.h2: What are the housing and income figures for Lenoir County?
sections.html:
Lenoir County had an estimated 55,837 residents on July 1, 2025, compared with 59,495 at the 2010 census. It has 27,402 housing units on 399.09 square miles of land.

The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 numbers show a median owner-occupied home value of $120,500 and an owner-occupancy rate of 59.2 percent, which leaves roughly 41 percent of homes as rentals. Median gross rent is $861, and median household income is $45,143. About 19.1 percent of people live in poverty, and 22.4 percent are 65 or older.

Median owner costs with a mortgage are $1,237 a month, and without one $460. At those values, a property tax bill makes up a large part of what a low-income owner pays each year, and a house with back taxes can lose most of its equity to the debt. Building permits numbered 131 in 2025, so there is little new construction competing with a resale in Kinston and the surrounding county.

faqs.q: Who do I call about property tax in Lenoir County?
faqs.a: Call the Lenoir County Tax Department at 252-527-7174. It is at 101 North Queen Street in Kinston and open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

faqs.q: When is the Lenoir County real estate appeal deadline?
faqs.a: The 2026 window closed April 23, 2026, when the Board of Equalization and Review adjourned. The county says the 2027 window opens January 1, 2027, and appeals must be made before the board adjourns.

faqs.q: Do I have to list my house with Lenoir County every year?
faqs.a: No. The county uses a permanent listing system for real estate, so real property does not need relisting unless its value changed. Personal property such as boats and unlicensed vehicles must be listed each January.

faqs.q: What is the late listing penalty in Lenoir County?
faqs.a: Ten percent. Personal property listings received after the January listing period, which ends January 31, are charged that penalty under state law.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lenoir County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes, but the tax is a lien on the parcel and is normally paid from sale proceeds at closing. Ask the tax office for the balance before you sign, so the payoff is on the settlement statement.
